input: Find bribery and corruption allegations involving Embraer, in Brazil and abroad

events.type: Foreign bribery (FCPA anti-bribery, books-and-records and internal-controls violations); deferred prosecution agreement
events.jurisdiction: United States (DOJ Fraud Section; U.S. District Court, S.D. Florida)
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; bribe recipients were officials in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia (state-owned company), Mozambique (LAM) and an agent in India
events.summary: Embraer admitted conspiring to violate the FCPA by paying US$3.52M (Dominican Republic, 2008), US$1.65M (Saudi Arabia, 2010), US$800K (Mozambique, 2008) and US$5.76M to an agent (India, 2009) through false agency agreements, which earned it nearly US$84M in profit; it agreed to a 3-year DPA with an independent monitor, and the penalty was set 20% below the guidelines minimum because remediation was incomplete.

events.parties: Embraer S.A. (payments routed through its U.S.-based subsidiary)
events.amount: More than US$98M disgorgement and interest (US$83.8M disgorgement + US$14.4M prejudgment interest), with up to US$20M credit for Brazilian disgorgement (as_of 2016-10-24)
events.summary: The SEC alleged that Embraer made more than US$83M in profit from bribes paid through third-party agents in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia and Mozambique, kept false books to hide them, and ran an accounting scheme in India; this was part of a global settlement of more than US$205M.

events.jurisdiction: United States (U.S. District Court, S.D. Florida)
events.summary: The court dismissed the FCPA charges against Embraer after finding it had fully complied with all obligations under its 2016 DPA; the monitorship had expired on 2020-05-22.

events.type: Bribery of foreign officials; settlement under Brazilian law (Termo de Compromisso e de Ajustamento de Conduta)
events.amount: R$64M (R$58M to the Fundo de Defesa dos Direitos Difusos + R$6M to the CVM) (as_of 2016-10-24)
events.summary: Embraer admitted bribing public officials in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique and India through intermediaries and false accounting records, including a sham commercial-representation contract in India; the CVM board approved the settlement on 2016-10-06 and the MPF's 5ª Câmara on 2016-10-20.

events.type: Active corruption in an international commercial transaction; money laundering (criminal prosecution of former executives)
events.jurisdiction: Brazil (7ª Vara Federal Criminal do Rio de Janeiro; TRF-2, 1ª Turma Especializada)
events.status: convicted (first instance); on appeal, time-barred for 8 executives and acquitted of money laundering; conviction upheld only for Eduardo Munhóz de Campos
events.parties: Former Embraer executives: Eduardo Munhóz de Campos (former VP), Orlando José Ferreira Neto, Acir Luiz de Almeida Padinha Júnior, Albert Philip Close, Luiz Alberto Lage da Fonseca, Luiz Eduardo Zorzenon Fumagalli, Eduardo Augusto Fernandes Fagundes, Ricardo Marcelos Bester, Flávio Rímoli, Luiz Carlos Siqueira Aguiar
events.amount: US$3.5M bribe (Dominican Republic Super Tucano sale)
events.summary: Judge Marcelo Bretas convicted ten former executives in 2018 (7 years for Munhóz, 6.5 years for the others) over US$3.5M in bribes to a Dominican Air Force colonel for eight Super Tucano aircraft; in 2022 the TRF-2 declared the corruption counts time-barred for eight appellants, acquitted all appellants of money laundering, and cut Munhóz's sentence to 2 years 6 months, replaced with restrictive-rights penalties.

events.type: Regulatory proceeding (breach of duty of diligence linked to bribery)
events.parties: Flávio Rímoli, former Executive VP for Legal Affairs of Embraer (Embraer itself was not a party, having settled in 2016)
events.summary: The CVM board unanimously acquitted Rímoli of failing to scrutinise a commercial-representation contract (Globaltix, linked to sales to Jordan) through which most of the Dominican bribe was allegedly routed.

events.type: Bribery of public officials (abbreviated criminal procedure against the company)
events.jurisdiction: Dominican Republic (Cuarto Juzgado de la Instrucción del Distrito Nacional)
events.amount: US$7M to the Dominican State, twice the bribe (as_of 2018-08-24)
events.summary: Embraer agreed to an abbreviated criminal trial and compensation of about US$7M for the US$3.5M in bribes paid for the 2009 Super Tucano sale, and undertook to disclose the payment mechanisms and recipients; its Brazilian employees could not be tried in the Dominican Republic because they had already been convicted in Brazil.

events.type: Bribery (passive): prosecution of the Dominican officials who allegedly received Embraer's bribes
events.jurisdiction: Dominican Republic (Tercera Cámara Penal, Corte de Apelación del Distrito Nacional)
events.parties: Pedro Rafael Peña Antonio (former Defense Minister), Col. Carlos Piccini Núñez, Daniel Aquino Hernández, 4D Business Group, Magycor; Embraer named as the bribe payer
events.summary: The appeals court revoked the September 2023 ruling that had closed the case for exceeding the maximum duration and sent it back to the Cuarto Tribunal Colegiado for a new trial; the defendants had been acquitted in May 2022 before a retrial was ordered in June 2023.

events.type: Foreign bribery (FCPA), wire fraud, money laundering, false statements: individual prosecution (Saudi Aramco)
events.parties: Colin Steven, former sales executive at Embraer (Embraer Executive Jets)
events.amount: US$25,000 fine + US$700 assessment; sentenced to time served
events.summary: Steven pleaded guilty to seven counts over a scheme to bribe a Saudi Aramco official to win a US$93M Embraer jet sale, in which he also took a kickback; DOJ separately said Saudi authorities had charged two individuals over the Saudi conduct.

events.type: Bribery / corruption of state airline officials (prosecution of recipients and intermediary)
events.status: convicted (Zucula, Zimba); acquitted (Viegas, statute of limitations/insufficient evidence); appeals announced
events.parties: Paulo Zucula (former Transport Minister), Mateus Zimba (intermediary), José Viegas (former LAM chair); Embraer as bribe payer
events.amount: US$800,000 bribe; MZN70.7M (about US$1.1M) compensation ordered (as_of 2021-09-14)
events.summary: Zucula and Zimba each received ten years for the US$800K bribe Embraer paid through the São Tomé shell company Xihivele so that LAM would buy two Embraer aircraft in 2009; Viegas was acquitted.

events.date: 2023-06-05 (CBI chargesheet; FIR registered after a preliminary enquiry opened in September 2016)
events.type: Bribery / kickbacks in defence procurement (Prevention of Corruption Act, criminal conspiracy)
events.status: charged (individuals); Embraer booked in the FIR
events.parties: Embraer and Interdev Pte Ltd booked in the FIR; chargesheet names Arvind Khanna, Gautam Khaitan and Anup Gupta; proceedings against Vipin Khanna dropped after his death
events.amount: US$5.76M alleged kickbacks; deal for three aircraft signed 2008-07-03 (about US$208M per DOJ)
events.summary: The CBI alleges kickbacks were routed in 2009 from Embraer subsidiaries to middleman Vipin Khanna through Singapore-based Interdev to influence DRDO officials on the AEW&C (EMB-145) deal, even though Indian procurement rules bar middlemen.

events.type: Money laundering (PMLA) linked to defence-deal kickbacks
events.jurisdiction: India (Enforcement Directorate; court in New Delhi)
events.parties: Embraer SA Brazil, Interdev Aviation Services Pte Ltd, KRBL Ltd, Anoop Kumar Gupta, Anurag Potdar and others
events.amount: US$5.76M kickbacks; about US$3.275M routed to KRBL DMCC Dubai; contract US$210M (per ED)
events.summary: The ED's chargesheet alleges that Embraer hired Vipin Khanna for the AEW&C contract and that kickbacks were laundered through sham agreements with Interdev and KRBL's Dubai subsidiary into India.

output.assessment: Embraer S.A. has an admitted record of foreign bribery from 2007 to 2011 in four countries (Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique, India), resolved by a global settlement of about US$205.5M with the US and Brazil; the US DPA was dismissed in November 2020 after a monitorship that ended satisfactorily, and no new allegations against the company surfaced in my searches of 2025-2026. Proceedings still open: India's CBI and ED cases, in which Embraer is named in the FIR and in the ED chargesheet (current trial status not found); the Dominican retrial of the officials who received the bribes, reinstated in December 2024 (no later ruling found); and the appeals in Mozambique.
